name: Daniel Negreanu
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first World Series of Poker bracelet in the $2,000 Pot Limit Hold'em event at the 1998 WSOP, becoming the youngest bracelet winner in history at the time.
early_history_summary: Born to Romanian immigrant parents in Toronto, Negreanu discovered gambling and pool hustling as a teenager, learning poker at age 15 and playing full-time in charity casinos by 16. He dropped out of high school one credit short of graduation and moved to Las Vegas at 21, where he initially lost his bankroll before rebuilding and mastering the game.
family_context_summary: Born to Romanian immigrant parents in Toronto; father worked as an electrician and sold confectionery, mother was a homemaker. Working-class family with no gambling background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early gambling immersion, pool halls, charity casinos, self-taught, numbers aptitude
evidence_summary: Negreanu grew up in a working-class Romanian immigrant household in Toronto with no family connection to poker. He began playing poker at 15, hustling in pool halls by 16, and dropped out of high school to play full-time. His direct immersion in gambling environments from a young age gave him thousands of hours of practical experience before his 1998 WSOP bracelet win at age 23. No formal mentor or family domain advantage is documented; his success appears largely self-created through early and intense domain repetition.
starting_point: Born to Romanian immigrant parents in Toronto; father was an electrician and confectionery seller, mother a homemaker. Working-class family.
current_position: Professional poker player with 8 WSOP bracelets, over $56M in live tournament winnings, and Poker Hall of Fame inductee; resides in Las Vegas.

trajectory.event: Won first WSOP bracelet in $2,000 Pot Limit Hold'em, becoming the youngest bracelet winner in history at the time and earning the nickname 'Kid Poker'.
Named WSOP Player of the Year and WPT Player of the Year after making 11 final tables and winning $4.4M in a single year.
Won two WSOP bracelets including the WSOP APAC Main Event, becoming the only player to win WSOP Player of the Year twice.
Inducted into the Poker Hall of Fame; recognized by Global Poker Index as the best poker player of the previous decade.
Won 8th WSOP bracelet in the $50,000 Poker Players Championship, ending an 11-year bracelet drought.

name: Arati Saha
milestone_by_age_26: Became the first Asian woman to swim across the English Channel on 29 September 1959 at age 19, completing the crossing in 16 hours 20 minutes.
early_history_summary: Saha learned to swim at age four at the Champatala Ghat in Calcutta and won her first gold medal at age five in 1946. Under the mentorship of Asian Games gold medalist Sachin Nag, she won 22 state-level competitions between 1945 and 1951 and competed at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics at age eleven, becoming the youngest Indian Olympian.
family_context_summary: Born into a middle-class Bengali family in Calcutta; father was an armed forces employee. Lost her mother at age two and was raised by her grandmother in North Kolkata.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No family swimming background identified.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Sachin Nag mentorship, Hatkhola Swimming Club, early swimming start, lost mother young, 22 state medals
evidence_summary: Saha was born into a middle-class family in Calcutta and lost her mother at age two, raised by her grandmother. She discovered swimming at age four at a public bathing ghat and was enrolled at Hatkhola Swimming Club, where Asian Games gold medalist Sachin Nag became her mentor. Nag's sustained coaching and her early start led to 22 state-level medals by age eleven and an Olympic appearance at the 1952 Helsinki Games. Her English Channel crossing at 19 was the culmination of 15 years of intensive swimming and dedicated mentorship.
starting_point: Born into a middle-class Bengali family in Calcutta; father was an armed forces employee. Lost mother at age two and was raised by grandmother.
current_position: Died in August 1994 at age 53 in Calcutta; final status: Padma Shri awardee and first Asian woman to swim the English Channel.

trajectory.event: Won first gold medal in 110 yards freestyle at the Shailendra Memorial Swimming Competition, beginning her competitive career.
Became the youngest Indian Olympian, competing in the 200m breaststroke at the Helsinki Olympics.
First Asian woman to swim across the English Channel, completing the crossing from France to England in 16 hours 20 minutes.
Awarded the Padma Shri, becoming the first Indian sportswoman to receive the honor.
Died in Calcutta on 23 August 1994.

name: Gina Gogean
milestone_by_age_26: Won floor exercise gold at the 1992 European Championships at age 13-14, establishing herself as one of the youngest senior continental champions in gymnastics history.
early_history_summary: Gogean trained at CSS Focsani under Sergiu and Tatiana Popa before being elevated to the Romanian junior national team at Onesti and the senior national team at Deva, coached by Octavian Bellu and Mariana Bitang. She made her international debut at the 1989 Japan Junior International at age 11, winning floor exercise gold, and was competing at the senior level by 1990.
family_context_summary: Born in Campuri, Vrancea, Romania; family background not well documented beyond early training at a local gymnastics club.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Romanian gymnastics system, CSS Focsani, Deva training center, Bellu and Bitang coaching, Milošovici teammate, early international debut
evidence_summary: Gogean was identified early and channeled through Romania's elite gymnastics pipeline: local club CSS Focsani, junior national team at Onesti, and senior national team at Deva under renowned coaches Octavian Bellu and Mariana Bitang. She made her international debut at 11 and was winning senior European Championship gold by 13-14. The Romanian gymnastics dynasty provided world-class coaching, facilities, and a competitive team environment with teammates like Lavinia Milošovici. Note: her birth year is disputed; hospital records indicate 1978 while official competition documents listed 1977.
starting_point: Born in Campuri, Vrancea, Romania; began gymnastics training at a local club before entering the Romanian national gymnastics pipeline.
current_position: Retired from gymnastics in 1998 at age 20; later worked as a gymnastics coach and international judge; inducted into the International Gymnastics Hall of Fame in 2013.

trajectory.event: Made international debut at Japan Junior International, placing fourth all-around and winning gold on floor exercise.
Won floor exercise gold at European Championships and Olympic team silver at Barcelona, establishing herself as a senior international gymnast.
Won European all-around title and led Romania to World Championship team gold.
Won Olympic all-around silver and three bronze medals at Atlanta despite an emergency appendectomy five weeks before the Games.
Won three gold medals at World Championships in Lausanne (floor, beam, team), the peak of her competitive career.
Retired from competitive gymnastics after the World Cup in Japan.
Inducted into the International Gymnastics Hall of Fame.

name: Jean Reno
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Reno's first film role came in 1979 at age 31; his breakthrough was Le Dernier Combat (1983) at age 35, and stardom arrived with The Big Blue (1988) at age 40.
early_history_summary: Born in Casablanca to Spanish parents who fled Francoist Spain, Reno moved to France at 17 and studied drama in Casablanca and Paris. He toured in stage productions through the late 1970s before his first film appearance in 1979.
family_context_summary: Born to Spanish parents in Casablanca, French Morocco; father was a linotypist, mother died when he was a teenager. Family moved to France when Reno was 17.
evidence_summary: Reno studied drama in Casablanca and Paris and toured French stage productions through the late 1970s, but did not appear in films until 1979 at age 31. His career breakthrough came through his collaboration with director Luc Besson in the 1980s. No material acting milestone by age 26 is documented.

name: Dmitry Muratov
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Muratov began working as a newspaper reporter in the mid-1980s; he co-founded Novaya Gazeta in 1993 at age 32 and became editor-in-chief in 1995. Nobel Peace Prize came in 2021.
early_history_summary: Muratov studied philology at Kuibyshev State University and began working as a correspondent for Volzhsky Komsomolets in 1987 at age 26. He later moved to Komsomolskaya Pravda before co-founding Novaya Gazeta in 1993.
family_context_summary: Born into a Russian family in Kuibyshev (now Samara), USSR. Family background not detailed in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Muratov discovered journalism in college and began his professional reporting career at Volzhsky Komsomolets in 1987 at age 26. His major achievements — co-founding Novaya Gazeta (1993), becoming editor-in-chief (1995), and winning the Nobel Peace Prize (2021) — all occurred well after age 26. No material career milestone by age 26 is documented.

name: Massoud Rajavi
milestone_by_age_26: No material positive milestone by age 26 found. Rajavi joined the MEK at 20 and became a Central Committee member, but was arrested by SAVAK and imprisoned through his mid-twenties. His leadership of MEK began in 1979 at age 31 after release from prison.
early_history_summary: Rajavi joined the People's Mojahedin Organization of Iran (MEK) in 1967 at age 20 while studying law at the University of Tehran. He became a Central Committee member but was arrested by SAVAK and sentenced to death, later commuted to life imprisonment. He remained in prison until the 1979 Iranian Revolution.
family_context_summary: Born in Tabas, South Khorasan, Iran; described as coming from a family of intellectuals. Brother Kazem Rajavi was a lawyer who helped commute his death sentence.
evidence_summary: Rajavi joined the MEK at age 20 and rose to its Central Committee, but was arrested by SAVAK and spent his twenties in prison. His leadership of the organization and major political milestones came after age 26, following his release during the 1979 Iranian Revolution. No positive material milestone by age 26 is documented; his twenties were defined by imprisonment.

name: Renzo Zorzi
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Zorzi began racing in Formula Three in September 1972 at age 25, but his first major result (Monaco F3 win) came in 1975 at age 28, and his F1 debut was also in 1975.
early_history_summary: The son of a miner from Ziano di Fiemme, Trentino, Zorzi worked as an engineer at Pirelli before beginning his motor racing career in 1972 in Italian Formula Three. His early races were unsuccessful, and it was not until 1975 that he achieved his breakthrough victory in the Monaco F3 support race.
family_context_summary: Born in Ziano di Fiemme, Trentino, Italy; son of a miner. Worked as an engineer at Pirelli before starting racing career.
evidence_summary: Zorzi was the son of a miner who worked as a Pirelli engineer before beginning racing in 1972 at age 25. His first races in Italian Formula Three were without reward. His breakthrough — victory in the Monaco F3 support race — came in 1975 at age 28, leading to his F1 debut. No material racing milestone by age 26 is documented.

name: Kylie Minogue
milestone_by_age_26: Released debut single 'The Loco-Motion' in 1987 at age 19, which hit #1 in Australia, and won the Gold Logie as the youngest recipient ever for her role in Neighbours, before her debut album Kylie reached #1 in the UK in 1988.
early_history_summary: Minogue began acting in Australian television at age 12, appearing in series like Skyways and The Henderson Kids. Her casting as Charlene Mitchell in the soap opera Neighbours in 1986 at age 18 made her a star in Australia and the UK. She transitioned to music in 1987, signing with Mushroom Records and releasing 'The Loco-Motion' as her debut single.
family_context_summary: Born in Melbourne to a middle-class family; father was a car company accountant, mother a former ballet dancer from Wales. Younger sister Dannii Minogue is also an actress and singer.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a former ballet dancer who encouraged the children's performing arts involvement; sister Dannii also pursued entertainment, creating a family domain immersion in performance.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Neighbours TV platform, Stock Aitken Waterman, early TV acting, sister Dannii, Australian soap opera to pop pipeline
evidence_summary: Minogue grew up in a middle-class Melbourne household with a mother who was a former ballet dancer and a sister who also entered entertainment. She began acting on Australian TV at 12 and leveraged the massive audience of Neighbours at 18 to launch a music career. Her signing with Mushroom Records and the Stock Aitken Waterman production team at 19 gave her a powerful distribution and production platform. The soap-opera-to-pop-star pipeline of the late 1980s was a structural wave she rode effectively, becoming the youngest Gold Logie winner and scoring a #1 debut single before age 20.
starting_point: Born in Melbourne to a middle-class family; father was a car company accountant, mother a former ballet dancer from Wales who emigrated to Australia at age 10.
current_position: Global pop icon with over 80 million records sold worldwide; highest-selling Australian-born female artist of all time; two-time Grammy winner; resides in London.

trajectory.event: Cast as Charlene Mitchell in the Australian soap opera Neighbours, becoming a star in Australia and the UK.
Released debut single 'The Loco-Motion' which hit #1 in Australia; won Gold Logie as youngest recipient ever for Neighbours.
Debut album Kylie reached #1 in the UK and sold over 5 million copies worldwide, establishing her as a pop star.
Released album Fever with global chart-topping single 'Can't Get You Out of My Head,' achieving worldwide pop superstardom.
Won first Grammy Award for Best Dance Recording for 'Come into My World.'
Won second Grammy for 'Padam Padam' and was named to Time's 100 Most Influential People list.

name: R. Murray Schafer

Schafer studied at the Royal Conservatory of Music and University of Toronto from 1952, left formal studies in 1955, and spent 1956-1960 in Vienna and England doing informal study and journalism. His first major organized concert series (Ten Centuries Concerts) came in 1961 at age 28.

He left formal studies in 1955 and traveled to Vienna and England, where he studied informally, worked as a journalist, and prepared a performing edition of Ezra Pound's opera. He returned to Toronto in 1961.
family_context_summary: Born in Sarnia, Ontario; father was an accountant for Imperial Oil. Family moved to Toronto in 1934. Mother encouraged the boys to join the choir at Grace Church on-the-Hill.

evidence_summary: Schafer studied music formally at the Royal Conservatory and University of Toronto from ages 19-22, then pursued autodidactic study and informal training in Vienna and England through his mid-twenties. His first significant career milestone — organizing the Ten Centuries Concerts series — came in 1961 at age 28. No material composition or career milestone by age 26 is documented.

name: Maurice Bishop
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Bishop completed his law degree in London in 1969 at age 25 and returned to Grenada in 1970 at age 26. His major political milestones — forming MAP (1972), co-founding the New JEWEL Movement (1973), and leading the Grenada Revolution (1979) — all occurred after age 26.
early_history_summary: Bishop won a scholarship to Presentation Brothers' College in Grenada, where he excelled and developed an interest in politics. He moved to London in 1963 to study law at the University of London and Gray's Inn, becoming president of the West Indian Students' Society and co-founding a legal aid clinic before completing his legal training in 1969.
family_context_summary: Born on Aruba to Grenadian parents; father Rupert worked in an oil refinery and later ran small businesses in Grenada. Family moved to Grenada in 1950. Bishop won a government scholarship for secondary education.
evidence_summary: Bishop was an academically gifted student who won a scholarship to Presentation Brothers' College and later studied law in London, where he was president of the West Indian Students' Society and co-founded a legal aid clinic. However, his major political achievements — forming the Movement for Assemblies of the People (1972), co-founding the New JEWEL Movement (1973), and leading the Grenada Revolution (1979) — all occurred after age 26. name: Shozo Tsugitani
milestone_by_age_26: Debuted for the Japan national football team on 15 August 1961 at age 21, and went on to earn 12 caps and score 4 goals for Japan between 1961 and 1965, also playing at the 1962 Asian Games.
early_history_summary: Tsugitani played football at Kwansei Gakuin High School (1956-58) and Kwansei Gakuin University (1959-62). While still a university student, he debuted for the Japan national team against Indonesia on 15 August 1961. After graduating, he joined Mitsubishi Motors in 1963 and played in the inaugural Japan Soccer League season in 1965.
family_context_summary: Born in Hyogo Prefecture, Japan. Family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Kwansei Gakuin University, Mitsubishi Motors, Japan national team, high school to university football
evidence_summary: Tsugitani played football through high school and university at Kwansei Gakuin, earning a call-up to the Japan national team at 21 while still a student. He represented Japan at the 1962 Asian Games and earned 12 caps through 1965. After university, he joined Mitsubishi Motors and played in the inaugural Japan Soccer League. His path was conventional — school to university to corporate club — with no documented family advantage or exceptional early resources. Japanese football was not yet developed as a professional sport during his era.
starting_point: Born in Hyogo Prefecture, Japan; family background not documented in reviewed sources. Attended Kwansei Gakuin High School and University.
current_position: Died in June 1978 at age 37 in Kobe, Hyogo; final role: former Japan international footballer and Mitsubishi Motors player.

trajectory.event: Debuted for the Japan national football team against Indonesia on 15 August while still a Kwansei Gakuin University student.
Represented Japan at the 1962 Asian Games.
Joined Mitsubishi Motors (New Mitsubishi Heavy Industries) after graduating from Kwansei Gakuin University.
Played in the inaugural Japan Soccer League season for Mitsubishi Heavy Industries.
Retired from active play; Mitsubishi Motors reached the Emperor's Cup final.
Died on 2 June 1978 in Kobe, Hyogo Prefecture.

name: Claude Cohen-Tannoudji
milestone_by_age_26: No material research milestone by age 26 found. Cohen-Tannoudji entered ENS in 1953, passed the agregation in 1957 at age 24, and began his doctoral thesis in 1959 at age 26. His first major research discovery (the light shift / optical Stark effect) came during his thesis work, defended in 1962 at age 29. Nobel Prize awarded in 1997.
early_history_summary: Cohen-Tannoudji was admitted second in the competitive entrance exam to the Ecole Normale Superieure in 1953 at age 20. He joined Alfred Kastler and Jean Brossel's research group in 1955, passed the agregation in 1957, and served in the military before beginning his doctoral thesis on optical pumping in 1959.
family_context_summary: Born in Constantine, Algeria to a modest Sephardic Jewish family; family moved to Algiers in 1938 to escape anti-Semitic violence. Experienced Vichy-era discrimination during WWII.
evidence_summary: Cohen-Tannoudji was a brilliant student who entered ENS at 20 (2nd in the competitive exam) and passed the agregation at 24, but these are academic qualifications rather than material research milestones. His first significant research contribution — the discovery of the light shift effect — came during his doctoral thesis, which he began at 26 and defended at 29. His Nobel Prize-winning work on laser cooling came decades later in the 1980s-1990s. No material independently verifiable research milestone by age 26 is documented.
